findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_companies, get_company_deadlines, get_company_finances, get_accounts_route_counts, find_companies, search_help · Private data: get_company_deadlines, get_company_finances, get_accounts_route_counts, find_companies, export_companies, validate_accounts, prepare_accounts, calculate_penalty, check_company_size, send_feedback, search_help · Public sink: follow_companies, send_feedback · Destructive: prepare_accounts, prepare_ct600, run_company_tools, send_feedback.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_companies, get_company_deadlines, get_company_finances, get_accounts_route_counts, find_companies, search_help · Private data: get_company_deadlines, get_company_finances, get_accounts_route_counts, find_companies, export_companies, validate_accounts, prepare_accounts, calculate_penalty, check_company_size, send_feedback, search_help · Public sink: follow_companies, send_feedback · Destructive: prepare_accounts, prepare_ct600, run_company_tools, send_feedback

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "search_companies" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
